meta.title: Telemavix - GPS tracks and telemetry overlays for action cameras | Sefinek
meta.description: Record GPS tracks on your phone and add speed, maps and other data to action camera and drone footage. Discover Telemavix GPS and Telemavix Studio.
meta.keywords: telemavix, telemetry overlay, gps track, fit, gpx, dji osmo action, gopro, dji drone, hud

softwareDescription: Telemavix GPS records routes and phone sensor data. Telemavix Studio adds overlays with speed, maps, tilt and other readings to your videos.
label: Project
heading: Telemavix
intro: Your footage can show more. Use Telemavix Studio to add a speedometer, route map, tilt indicator and other widgets. Customize their appearance, arrange them on your video and show your activity from a new perspective. Use data from your camera or drone, or record your route on your phone with Telemavix GPS.

videos.intro: Example videos with Telemavix Studio widgets. Choose a video to watch it on YouTube. The app keeps evolving, so some widgets may already look different in the current version.

steps.title: 1. Record your activity
steps.text: Film your activity with an action camera or drone. To record your route on your phone, start Telemavix GPS. With a supported DJI Osmo Action camera, you can start and stop track recording at the same time as video recording. The app replaces the DJI GPS Bluetooth Remote Controller, so you do not need to buy one.

steps.title: 2. Open the footage in Studio
steps.text: Telemavix Studio reads the available data saved by a supported camera. You can also add a FIT or GPX file from Telemavix GPS, a sports watch or a bike computer, such as a Garmin device. If your DJI drone does not store telemetry in the footage, add a flight log.

steps.title: 3. Add an overlay and save your video
steps.text: Choose your widgets and arrange them on the video. If you use a separate track file, check its alignment with the footage. Watch the preview, then export your finished video.

mobile.title: Telemavix GPS for your phone
mobile.text: Records your route and readings from available phone sensors. Shows speed, distance, moving time and elevation changes. Recording continues with the screen off, and previously loaded map areas remain available offline. It works as a GPS remote for supported DJI Osmo Action cameras, replacing the DJI GPS Bluetooth Remote Controller.

desktop.title: Telemavix Studio for your computer
desktop.text: Adds video overlays using data from your camera, a track file or a flight log. Arrange widgets, trim your footage and add music. The Windows version is regularly tested; Linux and macOS versions are experimental.

download.title: Download Telemavix Studio
download.intro: Pick the file for your system. If you are not sure which one to choose, use the installer on Windows. Current version: {{version}}.
download.cpuHelp: Not sure which processor you have? On Windows, go to Settings > System > About and check System type. On Linux and macOS, run `uname -m`: x86_64 means x64, while arm64 or aarch64 means ARM64.
download.runtimeHelp: If you choose the version that requires .NET, install the [.NET 10 Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) for your system and processor. Studio also needs FFmpeg 9 and offers to install it on first launch if it is missing. Linux and macOS versions are experimental.
download.more: All files, checksums and release notes are on the [releases page]({{releasesUrl}}).

features.title: What you can do in Telemavix Studio

items.title: Export with the original settings
items.text: By default, Studio keeps the original resolution, codec, color depth and bitrate, including for 10-bit footage. Adding an overlay requires re-encoding the video. Keeping the source settings helps limit quality loss.

items.title: Processing on your computer
items.text: Your video is processed on your computer. Studio can use a supported graphics card to speed up export. Keep the original settings or choose an export profile for how you plan to share the video.

items.title: Data recorded by your camera
items.text: Studio reads available data from your footage, such as GPS position, speed, camera motion and exposure settings. Available readings depend on the model and how you record. If your camera splits a recording into several files, you can join them into one video.

items.title: Tracks from phones, watches and drones
items.text: Import a FIT or GPX file from Telemavix GPS, a sports watch or a bike computer, such as a Garmin device. Alongside the route, Studio reads available data such as speed, elevation, heart rate, cadence and battery level. You can also add flight logs for supported DJI drones. Synchronize the data with your footage so the readings match what you see in the video.

items.title: Customize your widgets
items.text: Choose a speedometer, map, compass, tilt indicator, G-meter or elevation chart. Drag widgets into place on the video and check the result in the preview. Available widgets depend on the data in your footage or track file.

items.title: Editing and music
items.text: Remove unwanted sections and add transitions and captions. Add music with fades and adjust the volume of the recording. You can open the video with a map and route summary.

items.title: A finished video or just the overlay
items.text: Save your video with the widgets included, or export just the overlay on a green background or with transparency for further editing. Queue several exports or automate them with the command-line tool.

items.title: Extra tools for your recordings
items.text: Remove metadata before sharing a video, fix color tags or compare the properties of up to six videos side by side. Convert a separate AAC file from the camera microphone to WAV or M4A for further editing.

devices.title: Supported devices
devices.intro: Check which devices you can use and where to get GPS data for your video. Open the original recordings from the memory card in Studio.
devices.note: In my experience, recording telemetry in DJI Mimo is cumbersome and unintuitive. Sometimes it is hard to tell whether recording is working at all. I recommend [Telemavix GPS](#apps) for recording routes and sensor data, especially if you have a supported DJI Osmo Action camera.

rows.notes: Tested models: Action 6 and Action 5 Pro. Other models in the series should work, but have not been tested yet.
rows.gps: Telemavix GPS or DJI GPS Bluetooth Remote Controller

rows.notes: This is the only GoPro model tested so far. Pitch has been checked against recorded footage, while roll still needs a controlled sideways tilt test.
rows.gps: An external FIT or GPX file, for example from Telemavix GPS. The HERO12 Black has no built-in GPS. GPS data from other GoPro models has not yet been verified with real recordings.

rows.notes: Supported models: Mavic Air 2, Mavic 4 Pro, Flip, Avata 360 and Lito X1 Plus.
rows.gps: Mavic Air 2, Mavic 4 Pro, Flip and Avata 360: a flight log (FlightRecord_*.txt) saved by the DJI Fly app. Lito X1 Plus: telemetry is stored in the footage, so you do not need to add a separate file.

rows.notes: Tested with the Garmin 7X. Studio also supports FIT files from Garmin bike computers.
rows.gps: A FIT activity file. Studio also reads heart rate, cadence and battery level when present in the file.
Add a FIT or GPX track. Studio does not yet read GPS data from this camera's recordings.
